segments.text: This is what happens when two planets collide.
Four and a half billion years ago, a planet the size of Mars smashed into Earth.
Scientists call it Theia. The crash was so violent, Earth's whole surface melted.
Rock boiled into vapor, and a giant cloud of glowing debris blasted into space.
The debris swirled around our planet in a burning ring.
Then it clumped together… into our Moon!
Some scientists think it took just a few hours.
Back then, the Moon was about 15 times closer than today.
And pieces of Theia may still be buried deep inside Earth.
So every time you see the Moon, you're seeing what happens when two planets collide.
